title: §23-001: B-Tree vs LSM-Tree Indexes & Query Execution Plans
description: Multiple-choice practice questions and deep runtime verification for §23-001 (B-Tree vs LSM-Tree Indexes & Query Execution Plans).

cards.concept: B-Tree vs LSM-Tree Indexes & Query Execution Plans: B-Tree vs LSM-Tree Storage Engines
cards.question: What is the primary architectural trade-off between B+ Tree (PostgreSQL) and LSM-Tree (Cassandra, RocksDB) storage engines?

options.text: B+ Trees only store integers; LSM-Trees only store JSON.

B+ Trees optimize read performance and point lookups at the cost of random write I/O; LSM-Trees optimize write throughput via sequential append-only logs and MemTables at the cost of read amplification.
LSM-Trees do not support disk storage.
B+ Trees require Redis to function.

cards.explanation: B+ Trees update pages in-place, incurring random write I/O but providing fast reads. LSM-Trees append writes sequentially to a write-ahead log and in-memory MemTable, delivering high write throughput.
cards.codeSnippet:
// B+ Tree: In-place page updates with WAL
// LSM-Tree: MemTable -> SSTable flush -> Background compaction
cards.pitfall: Indexing every column with B+ Trees severely degrades INSERT/UPDATE write throughput due to tree rebalancing.
cards.citation: Designing Data-Intensive Applications (Chapter 3: Storage and Retrieval)

cards.concept: B-Tree vs LSM-Tree Indexes & Query Execution Plans: Cache-Aside Pattern & Cache Stampede
cards.question: What is a 'cache stampede' (dogpiling), and how is it mitigated when implementing the Cache-Aside pattern with Redis?

options.text: Redis runs out of physical RAM and crashes.
When a heavily requested cache key expires, thousands of concurrent requests simultaneously miss the cache and query the database at once; mitigate with TTL jitter or mutex locking.
Network latency exceeds 100ms.
Clients write duplicate keys to the cache.

cards.explanation: Cache stampede occurs when key expiry causes simultaneous database queries. Adding randomized TTL jitter (e.g. 5m +/- 30s) prevents synchronized mass expiration across cached items.
cards.pitfall: Using fixed identical TTLs for batch-cached entities causes all keys to expire simultaneously, triggering stampedes.
cards.citation: Redis Best Practices: Avoiding Cache Stampedes
